display.purpose: The single big status word on AD Command (HOLD / READY TO ROLL / ROLLING) — the only place the system permits real scale.

label.purpose: Uppercase section eyebrows and stat labels — signage caption, not a heading.

data.purpose: Every operationally-live number: timestamps, elapsed hold, take counts, readiness percentage. Tabular numerals.

motion.name: fade-in
motion.purpose: New content appearing in place (e.g. generated task cards).

motion.name: slide-in
motion.purpose: New Agent Activity log entries arriving.

motion.name: pulse-lamp
motion.purpose: The unread-hold indicator dot on the My Set nav item.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one confident action on a screen — Clear Hold, Roll Camera, Lighting Ready.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><path d="M20 6 9 17l-5-5"/></svg>Clear Hold</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; background:#17181a; color:#fff; border:1px solid transparent; border-radius:2px; padding:10px 18px; font-family:'Zen Kaku Gothic New',sans-serif; font-size:13px; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:0.01em; cursor:pointer; transition:all .12s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:#000; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #c81e2c; outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform:scale(0.98); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background:#ffffff; color:#17181a; border:1px solid #c3bca8; border-radius:2px; padding:10px 18px; font-family:'Zen Kaku Gothic New',sans-serif; font-size:13px; font-weight:600; cursor:pointer; transition:all .12s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background:#eeece4; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #c81e2c; outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Status Lamp Pill
components.description: The signature status indicator: a solid andon lamp dot leading an uppercase label, never a plain rounded chip.
components.css: .ds-pill { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:7px; padding:3px 9px 3px 7px; border-radius:2px; font-family:'Zen Kaku Gothic New',sans-serif; font-size:11px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:0.06em; text-transform:uppercase; background:#e2eeec; color:#0f4f45; border:1px solid rgba(20,99,86,0.18); } .ds-lamp { width:6px; height:6px; border-radius:50%; background:#146356; flex-shrink:0; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat container, hairline border, no shadow — the base unit of every page.
components.css: .ds-card { background:#ffffff; border:1px solid #ded8c8; border-radius:3px; padding:24px; transition:border-color .15s; } .ds-card:hover { border-color:#c3bca8; }

components.name: Nav Item
components.description: Rail navigation item with a subway-style red rule marking the active page, not a filled rounded background.
components.html: <button class="ds-nav-link ds-nav-link--active"><svg width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><rect x="3" y="3" width="18" height="18" rx="2"/></svg>AD Command</button>
components.css: .ds-nav-link { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:12px; padding:10px 14px; border-left:2px solid transparent; color:#9a9b9e; font-family:'Zen Kaku Gothic New',sans-serif; font-size:13px; font-weight:500; background:none; border-top:none; border-right:none; border-bottom:none; width:100%; cursor:pointer; transition:all .12s; } .ds-nav-link:hover { background:rgba(255,255,255,0.04); color:#e8e8e6; } .ds-nav-link--active { background:rgba(200,30,44,0.1); color:#fff; border-left-color:#c81e2c; }

narrative.overview:
On Cue is a film-set readiness board, not an ops dashboard with a film theme painted on. Its visual world comes from the two Japanese operations-floor systems built for exactly its problem — status legible at a glance, under bad light, by someone with no time to read: the andon board (the manufacturing-floor lamp system where a colored light communicates line status before any word does) and JR rail departure signage (dense, disciplined, high-legibility information design that has never needed a drop shadow to feel authoritative). Both are minimalist by function, not by decoration.
The system deliberately refuses the default AI-generated ops-dashboard look it replaced: soft rounded cards floating on drop shadows, a teal-accent SaaS palette, pill badges, a generic dark sidebar. Line and space carry hierarchy here. Color is a signal, spent narrowly and precisely, never a decoration spread across a surface. Status renders as a small solid lamp — the andon light — never a rounded chip.
keyCharacteristics: Flat surfaces, hairline borders, zero box-shadow — depth from line weight and spacing, never blur.
Sharp, nearly-square corners (2-3px) everywhere except true circles.
One saturated red carries every stop/blocker signal.
Status is a small colored dot beside a label, never a colored border strip on a card edge.
Zen Kaku Gothic New for all text; JetBrains Mono for every number that means something.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Red is the only color allowed to mean "stop." No other red-family value, no orange escalation tier.

rules.name: The Lamp, Not the Chip Rule
rules.body: Status never renders as a fully-rounded pill badge alone. A small solid-color circle (the andon lamp) leads every status indicator.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Live Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for numbers a crew member would act on — a target time, an elapsed hold, a take count.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow appears anywhere in the system. A card separates from its neighbor by a hairline border and by the paper showing through the gap, never by a drop shadow.

dos: Do lead every status communication with a solid-color lamp (dot) before the word.
Do keep corners sharp (2-3px) except true circles.
Do reserve Signal Red for stop/blocker/destructive meaning only.
Do set every time, count, or take number in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals.
Do separate cards with a hairline border and paper showing through the gap.
donts: Don't add box-shadow to any surface.
Don't render status as a fully-rounded pill with no lamp.
Don't use a colored left-border strip as a card's status accent.
Don't introduce a second display typeface.
Don't use SaaS teal for "ready" — the system's go-signal is the blue-shifted shingou green.
